messages:
jordan: Heads-up — sample app hit a weird combo of 408 timeouts + token-refresh retries on Android. Seen it on Pixel 5 + emulator. Repro steps at the end.
alyssa: ugh. stack traces or logs? any pattern?
jordan: logs show request -> 408 (okhttp) -> our interceptor calls refresh -> retries -> new request gets 401 -> interceptor refresh again -> retry -> eventually succeeds after 3 tries or times out. Seems like a retry+auth race.
mike: that smells like doing sync refresh inside an interceptor. OkHttp's retry/follow-up machinery might re-use or drain the body incorrectly for non-idempotent requests. Do you have the interceptor code?
jordan: yep, simplified below:```kotlin
class AuthInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer ${'$'}{tokenProvider.get()}" )
      .build()
    val resp = chain.proceed(req)
    if (resp.code == 401) {
      tokenProvider.refreshSync()
      val retryReq = req.newBuilder()
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${'$'}{tokenProvider.get()}" )
        .build()
      return chain.proceed(retryReq)
    }
    return resp
  }
}
```
leo: this is the classic anti-pattern. Interceptor is fine for injecting auth header, but using it to synchronously refresh+retry can conflict with okhttp's RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor. Use an Authenticator for 401 (it gets the challenge and is called only when credentials fail). Also make refresh idempotent/threadsafe.
alyssa: +1. Authenticator example:```kotlin
val authenticator = Authenticator { route, response ->
  // only refresh once per challenge
  synchronized(tokenProvider) {
    if (response.request.header("Authorization")?.contains(tokenProvider.get()) == true) {
      tokenProvider.refreshSync()
      return@Authenticator response.request.newBuilder()
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${'$'}{tokenProvider.get()}")
        .build()
    }
  }
  null
}
client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(authenticator)
  .addInterceptor(AuthHeaderOnlyInterceptor(tokenProvider))
  .build()
```
mike: also check streaming requests (file upload / long polling) — those bodies are not rewindable. If okhttp retries them you will hit EOF or a 408. For non-idempotent operations, disable automatic retries or mark them so you don't re-send. We added a small helper in the SDK: `Request.tag(NonRetryable::class.java)` and `RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor` checks it.
jordan: good call. The repro includes a stubbed long-poll that sometimes returns 408 during network flaps, then our interceptor refresh kicks in and we double-send a streaming body which fails.
alyssa: Android gotcha: on older devices/okhttp versions TLS handshake + keepalive can cause spurious 408s if connection is reused. Try `connectionPool` tweaks and `pingInterval` on websocket-like flows. Also set conservative timeouts on the call: `.callTimeout(45, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` so SDK users don't hit platform default.
leo: small DX note: our Kotlin sample app was using a `synchronized` that locked the UI thread during refresh (whoops). We should show a non-blocking pattern in the sample: refresh via single-thread executor + suspend coroutine to avoid blocking.
devex-bot: New sample branch created: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-android/branch/kv-auth-fix — includes Authenticator + non-rewindable tag + docs. :white_check_mark:
jordan: will update our android-sample and open PR. Repro steps I used: 1) start emulator on poor network (toggle airplane mode briefly) 2) call endpoint that streams small file 3) return 408 from stub server on first attempt 4) token expired (401) on second attempt 5) observe interceptor refresh loop in logs.
mike: thx — when you open PR ping me, I'll review the interceptor -> authenticator migration and add a test for non-rewindable bodies.
jordan: thanks all, PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-android/pull/842 — includes changelog + migration guide.
alyssa: nice. add a short blurb in onboarding docs about "if your requests are non-idempotent, disable automatic retries and prefer Authenticator for 401 flows".
jordan: will do. Closing thread after PR merges. :tada:
